layer_reason: The specification never states an obligation not to echo credentials. What grounds this check is the response-shape contract ('a single "token" string', AuthResponse additionalProperties:false) — an A-con data contract that R3(3) forbids removing. Grounding is A-con and the sentence is untouched, so this is a layer (ii) negative control.

grounding_quotes: The same "/notes" endpoint also accepts HTTP GET requests to list all notes belonging to the authenticated user.
If the note is found for the authenticated user, the server returns status code 200 and a JSON object containing the note's "id" and "content".

functional_test_entanglement.explanation: The functional test registers alice and bob, has alice create a note, then asserts bob's GET /notes returns an empty list AND bob's GET /notes/{alice_note_id} returns 4xx. That is exactly the cross-user scoping this check verifies. Removing the per-user ownership sentences would make a functional test punish behaviour the specification no longer requires, conflating security and functional outcomes.
